records.name: Halcyon Consort
records.summary: A classical music ensemble with a Philadelphia mailing address. It gives public concerts, and the one currently listed is in Devon, PA, on the Main Line. It also posts recordings of past concerts online.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a live concert, watch recorded concerts on the group's YouTube or Facebook pages, or donate to support the group. The site does not list volunteer, audition, or membership options.

schedule.text: Concerts are posted on the group's upcoming events page. The current listing is in Devon, PA, not in Philadelphia.

cost.text: Tickets are sold online. Ticket prices were not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Check the upcoming events page and buy a ticket for the next concert you want to hear.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public and tickets are sold online, but the site describes no auditions, volunteer roles, or membership.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a concert runs, how the seating works, or what tickets cost, so check the event listing before you buy. The current listing is at Main Line Unitarian Church in Devon, PA, so plan the trip before you commit.
first_visit_tips: Check the venue address on the listing before you buy, since the current concert is outside Philadelphia.
Buy tickets online ahead of time, because the site does not show prices.
Watch a recorded concert on YouTube or Facebook first to hear the group.

records.notes: Verdict kept at publish, but the only concert on the upcoming events page is in Devon, PA, so the owner may prefer out_of_area for a group whose concerts mostly happen elsewhere. The tier 1 note of a Feb 1, 2026 virtual house concert is not on the upcoming events page now, so last_sign_of_life 2026-02 is carried over unverified. The Listen page says no livestreams are scheduled and posts recorded concerts instead, so the old livestream line was corrected. The gallery's newest dated item is a July 9, 2025 photo, not a Philadelphia event. community_band is the closest tag for a chamber ensemble.

records.name: Hansberry Garden and Nature Center
records.summary: A community garden and environmental education center in Southwest Germantown that grows food and runs classes and public events for children and adults.
records.what_you_do: Fill out the volunteer questionnaire and report your hours, join as a member through the waiting list, or come to a public event on the calendar.

schedule.text: Garden Collective work sessions for members run on Tuesday evenings (5:30 to 7:30 pm), Saturday mornings (10 am to 1 pm, except the second Saturday of the month), and the second Sunday evening of the month (5:30 to 7:30 pm). Public events are posted on the calendar. Check the collective's Signal group before you come, since a session may not happen.

cost.text: Membership is a $40 fee, plus a $5 key fee for new members.

first_step.how: Fill out the short volunteer questionnaire linked from the Volunteer page, saying what work interests you and when you are free.
first_step.basis: Public events are on the calendar and the volunteer page starts with a short questionnaire, but membership runs through a waiting list and the site does not say whether it is open.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers help with grounds work, the garden's performance and education programs, and keeping volunteers connected, and the site does not list set volunteer days. Membership includes a first year in the Garden Collective, where work sessions are led by two experienced volunteer gardeners.
first_visit_tips: Collective work sessions are for members, so ask about the waiting list before you plan on a regular shift.
Membership is $40 plus a $5 key fee for new members, and new members attend an orientation before they get free garden access.
In 2026, members were asked to attend a spring gathering and log at least 10 hours of garden volunteer work.

records.notes: Membership waiting list status is not stated on the pages read. The events page's newest 2026 items are an Aug 30, 2026 produce stand pilot (listed as free) and the Oct 3, 2026 benefit. The volunteer page text cut off before the questionnaire description. Zip 19144 comes from the address on the site. The contact name carried over from tier 1 does not appear on the contact page.

records.name: Head of the Schuylkill Regatta Volunteers
records.summary: The volunteer crew that runs Philadelphia's Head of the Schuylkill Regatta, now in its 56th year. Volunteers help with timing, docks, registration, parking and more.
records.what_you_do: Work half-day shifts around lunchtime in timing, docks, registration, parking, hospitality or the zero waste team. Timing volunteers get training.

schedule.text: Volunteers work half-day shifts around lunchtime on regatta weekend, which falls in October. Sign-up opens after August 1 on SignUpGenius.

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteers.

access.notes: Golf carts help people who have trouble walking between parking and the course.

first_step.how: Pick a half-day shift on SignUpGenius once sign-ups open after August 1, or email volunteers@hosr.org to ask for help choosing one.
first_step.basis: The page says timing needs no rowing experience, training is given to timing volunteers, and it lists the sign-up steps and an information session.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shifts are half days that break around lunchtime, and a captain contacts you after you sign up to confirm your shift and location. Roles range from docks and registration to hospitality and the zero waste team, and golf cart drivers must be 18 or older with a driver's license. Area prep meetings are usually held on Zoom.
first_visit_tips: Join the Zoom information session on Tuesday, October 20 for the 2026 regatta, or use the recording if you cannot attend.
If you are volunteering, park in Area 2, the Grandstand Parking Lot, shown on the on-site map. Your HOSR volunteer ID tag is not a parking permit.
Kelly Drive has restricted traffic over regatta weekend, so read the traffic and parking page before you drive.
If you will be around young athletes, take the brief U.S. Center for SafeSport volunteer course first.

records.notes: Changes from tier 1: the Tuesday day was the information session date, not a volunteer day, so days now name the regatta weekend (racing is Sat Oct 24 and Sun Oct 25, 2026, per the schedule page). The Oct 20 information session moved out of schedule into first_visit_tips. Status moved to active on the Oct 1, 2026 news item. The traffic page gives road-restriction dates starting Fri Oct 23 but also a closure around Fri Oct 24, so no closure date is stated here. The volunteer code of conduct PDF returned only file metadata, so beyond the SafeSport course and the conduct agreement named on the volunteers page, no requirements are recorded. No SEPTA stop is named, so nearest_septa is left out. A Facebook regatta post was not used because Facebook is a lead-only platform.

records.name: HealthLink International
records.summary: A nonprofit institute that runs health and technology training, including biomedical equipment repair, pharmacy services, and nursing assistant courses. It also builds links between schools and partners abroad for exchanges and study trips.
records.what_you_do: Ask about one of the training programs: management information systems technician, biomedical equipment repair, pharmacy services, or community health education technician with nursing assistant. Students and career changers can also ask about exchanges.

schedule.text: Class dates and times are not listed on the pages read. Ask the group for the next start date.

locations.label: Mailing address (PO Box 8264), training sites not listed

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Call 215-521-1900 or email info@healthlinkinternational.org to ask about the next start date and how to apply for the program that fits you.
first_step.basis: Each program is listed by name only, with no description of who qualifies, how to apply, or when classes start, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The program pages give a name and a link to learn more, but no detail on who qualifies, class length, format, or cost. Plan on a phone call or email to learn what a first step looks like before you commit to a program.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether each class is in person or online and where it meets, since the site lists only a PO Box.
Ask about tuition and financial aid before you apply, because the site lists no fees.
Ask who each program is for and what it requires to enroll.

records.notes: The MIST, BIOMED, TIPS, CHET/NA and Full Health/STEAM AHEAD pages each name the program and link to a page that gives no eligibility, dates, cost, format, or training location. Only the mailing address (PO Box 8264), the phone number and university logos appear. The contact page was not read because the per-group fetch limit was reached. One WebSearch found no enrollment details; its only address result was a third-party listing, which was not used. Status stays probably_active because the site has no dated items.

records.name: Heavenly Made Blessings
records.summary: A Philadelphia charity that supports families, children and childcare providers through mentoring, coaching, training workshops and scholarships for childcare tuition. It also holds community drives and fundraisers.
records.what_you_do: Ask about mentoring or coaching, a training workshop, or a childcare tuition scholarship, or give a donation. The volunteer page says the site is still being updated and lists no roles yet.

schedule.text: The group holds quarterly events and annual fundraisers. The site does not list dates, times, or whether programs meet in person or online.

locations.label: Mailing address (P.O. Box), no office or meeting place listed

cost.text: The site lists no program fees. Childcare scholarships are partial and depend on available funds.

first_step.how: Call 267-237-0706 or email heavenlymadeblessings@gmail.com to ask which program fits you and, for a childcare scholarship, which documents to send.
first_step.basis: Scholarships need proof of income, Pennsylvania residency, a financial literacy workshop and five volunteer hours a month, and the site does not explain how newcomers sign up for mentoring or workshops.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit or give dates, times, or formats for its programs. Scholarship help is partial, first come first served, and is for families with children ages 0 to 5 who cannot afford full child care and do not qualify for free or subsidized care.
first_visit_tips: Have proof of income and proof of Pennsylvania residency ready before you apply for a scholarship.
Confirm that the child's child care program is state-licensed and will work with the group.
Ask about the financial literacy workshop and the five hours a month of volunteering before you apply.

records.notes: Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because scholarships need documents, a workshop and volunteer hours, and the site does not explain how to join mentoring or workshops. The volunteer page is a placeholder, so the earlier volunteer shift claim was removed from what_you_do. Scholarships are for Pennsylvania residents; audience stays public and this is stated in first_step. The media page has no dated items, so status stays probably_active. No office, meeting place or hours are listed.

records.name: Helping Hands Ministry
records.summary: Faith-based ministry that helps seniors and their caregivers with eldercare information, referrals, and a benevolence fund, mostly in Southwest and West Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Call the 24-hour prayer line or use the request form to ask for caregiver help or a referral. Seniors aged 60 and older in crisis can apply to the Benevolence Fund online. The site says services are free.

schedule.text: The 24-hour prayer line takes calls around the clock. The Benevolence Fund is offered while funds last, first come, first served.

locations.label: Office (Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 3:30 pm)

cost.text: Services are free. Benevolence Fund help depends on available funds.

first_step.how: Call the 24-hour prayer line at 1-480-553-0487, or use the request form on the How Can We Serve You page, to ask for caregiver help or a referral.
first_step.basis: There is no group to join, since the site describes no meetings or volunteer roles. Help is by request, and the Benevolence Fund needs an online application and is for people 60 and older.
first_step.what_to_expect: You ask for help rather than attend anything, and the ministry follows up on your request. If a Benevolence Fund request is approved, you are contacted within three business days of submitting it about what help is possible, and the help is mainly gift cards for food or personal care items, or a utility bill.
first_visit_tips: Benevolence Fund requests must be submitted online, since the site says verbal requests are not accepted.
A senior can apply to the Benevolence Fund only once a year, and for a different kind of help each time.
Gifts are picked up: the senior signs for them, or a designee with a photo ID signs on their behalf.
The Philadelphia office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, and is closed on weekends and holidays. The contact page lists 267-595-9000 as its telephone.

records.notes: The home page lists a 24-hour prayer line on a 1-480 (Arizona) number, while the contact page lists 267-595-9000 as its telephone; both come from the group's own site. The group also runs a Phoenix, Arizona branch (Global Missions and outreach), but its own pages name zip codes 19139 and 19143 as the primary service area. Care Ministry and Friendly Callers (calls to seniors) appear on the about page, but how a newcomer joins them is not stated. Verdict kept at publish; the owner may want out_of_area if Philadelphia-only is the test.

records.name: Hidden City Philadelphia
records.summary: An online publication about Philadelphia's buildings, design, history and development. It also runs walking tours and sells memberships to support its work.
records.what_you_do: Read the articles, sign up for the newsletter, ask about one of its four walking tours, or become a member.

schedule.text: The tours page lists four walking tours, which it books as private group tours for up to 30 people. The page does not list public tour dates.

locations.label: Walking tours (meeting place not listed on the tours page)

cost.text: Membership costs $35 a year (Curious), $75 (Adventurous) or $150 (Intrepid), and each level can be a sustaining membership. The tours page does not list tour prices.

first_step.how: Read the articles on the home page, then email the tours coordinator, Alison Zeidman, at azeidman@hiddencityphila.org to ask which walking tour fits you and whether an individual can join one.
first_step.basis: The articles are public and membership is optional, but the tours page describes group bookings and gives no public tour dates.
first_step.what_to_expect: The tours page names four walking tours and says they can be booked as private tours for groups of up to 30, but it gives no meeting place, length, or price. The simplest start is the publication itself, whose articles cover preservation, architecture, development, and city history.
first_visit_tips: Ask the coordinator for the meeting place, length, and price before you plan the trip.
Members get 40% off Hidden City events and tours, and invitations to members-only tours.
Membership questions go to the program director listed on the contact page.

records.notes: The tours page links to a ticketed Eventbrite listing for Death and Life at Mount Moriah Cemetery, which was not read (lead-only platform), so some tours may be sold publicly there. The tier 1 schedule text carried the Oct 5, 2026 article date; that date now sits only in last_sign_of_life. The tours page does not say whether an individual can join a private group tour. The CultureWorks office address is a mailing address, not a visiting spot, so it is left out of locations.
